published.title: Whistleblowing reports to the SRA protected under PIDA
published.summary: The SRA is a prescribed person under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998. This means people who work for or with SRA-regulated firms are legally protected when they report wrongdoing to the SRA.

published.title: All firms holding client money to submit annual accountants' reports
published.summary: The SRA has asked the LSB to approve rules requiring every firm that holds client money to submit an annual accountants' report and declaration to the SRA. Fixed penalties would apply for late or missing reports.

published.title: Expanded supervision guidance for litigation work after Mazur judgment
published.summary: The SRA has expanded its supervision guidance after the Court of Appeal ruled in Mazur on what non-regulated staff can do under supervision when conducting litigation. It advises firms to check their arrangements are lawful.

published.title: New rules on keeping clients informed about their complaints proposed
published.summary: The SRA has proposed rules that would require firms to give clients a timeline for resolving a complaint and regular updates on its progress. Final proposals go to the LSB for approval.

published.title: Stronger rules on third-party litigation funding in consumer claims proposed
published.summary: The SRA has proposed new requirements for firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding in consumer claims. These include notifying the SRA, a risk assessment and summary documents for clients.

published.title: Warning notice on safe and responsible use of AI by law firms
published.summary: The SRA has issued a warning notice about misuse of AI. It reminds firms that their professional obligations stay the same when they use AI, and that it expects them to have proper oversight and controls.

published.title: Mandatory learning records and annual ethics discussions for solicitors proposed
published.summary: The SRA has proposed rules requiring solicitors to record their learning and development and take part in annual ethics discussions. Any rule changes would need Legal Services Board approval.

published.title: FCA to take over AML supervision of law firms: final policy set
published.summary: The government has set its final policy on how the FCA will supervise anti-money laundering compliance in professional services firms, including law firms. Legislation is still needed and no start date has been given.

published.title: New sanctions regime for human rights and humanitarian law violations
published.summary: The Global Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Sanctions Regulations 2026 came into force on 15 October 2026. They allow asset freezes and other sanctions against people involved in serious abuses.

published.title: Higher costs disclosure threshold and updated shortform disclosure forms
published.summary: The Legal Services Council has proposed raising the upper costs disclosure threshold to $10,000 and replacing the shortform disclosure forms under the Uniform General Rules.

published.title: AML/CTF obligations extended to lawyers providing designated services
published.summary: From 1 July 2026, law practices and lawyers providing designated services must enrol with AUSTRAC and comply with the anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing regime.

published.title: Updated guidance on NDAs in workplace sexual harassment matters
published.summary: The VLSB+C has updated its guidance on NDAs in workplace sexual harassment matters after a new Victorian Act commenced on 1 July 2026. It warns that lawyers who breach the Act's requirements could face disciplinary action.

published.title: Guidance on passing AML/CTF compliance costs on to clients
published.summary: The Legal Services Council has published an information sheet on how law practices treat AML/CTF compliance costs and when they can pass them on to clients.

updated.title: Stronger rules on third-party litigation funding proposed
updated.summary: The SRA has proposed new rules for firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding. Most apply only to consumer claims, but core conduct duties would apply to all funded claims. The consultation closed on 17 September 2026.
updated.event: Consultation closed on 17 September 2026. The SRA is analysing responses before deciding whether to seek LSB approval.
